This PR updates the `lastmod` timestamp on a contact when a new message is received.

The mobile app will sync the contact when a new contact message or room server message is received, and this timestamp change will help to push the contact to the top of the list.

I've been treating `lastmod` as a "last heard" timestamp. Currently, when new messages are received, the contact could stay at the bottom of the list, since it's sorted by `lastmod` by default.

author: l-kent
body:
Handles #271

In cases where there are non-returning indirect branches to other procedures, the frontend will now treat these as calls to those procedures (previously they were not handled or treated as GoTos which did not work), followed by Unreachable as R30 is not set to point to the following block.

Further work still needs to be done to handle these calls more accurately. This approach should be sound, but it should be possible to improve things with an analysis that identifies what R30 points to when these procedures have a Return statement, and adjust the control flow appropriately. The simplest case, which is the only one we've encountered so far, is tail calls, where R30 is set to be the input R30 to the calling procedure, so when the callee returns it just jumps to the callsite of the calling procedure (skipping a level, basically). I think constructing a heuristic to deal specifically with this case shouldn't be too difficult.

I haven't tested this much due to not having any suitable examples on hand - it seems to work but I haven't dug into whether the output is exactly what it should be because none of the examples in #271 are really suitable for more extensive investigation unfortunately (in one case the relevant procedure isn't actually called anywhere and is optimised out, in the other the resulting .bpl is multiple GB)

```bash
# Developer modifying protected-configs/prod.yml would see:
❌ ACCESS DENIED: Developers cannot modify PROTECTED paths content
❌ exit 1 - PR blocked
```

**After (Path Protection Stopped):**
```bash
# Same developer now sees:
✅ PATH PROTECTION DISABLED: All developers now have full access
✅ PR approved - path protection has been stopped
```

- `protected-configs/` - Configuration files with secrets
- `scripts/deployment/` - Production deployment scripts  
- `secrets/` - Secret files

- Updated `README` to clearly state path protection status
- Added comments to protected files demonstrating they're now accessible
- Modified `protected-configs/prod.yml` and `scripts/deployment/deploy.sh` as proof of concept

The workflow still runs on PRs but now always succeeds regardless of which files are modified. Both admin and developer users receive informational messages indicating that path protection has been stopped and all paths are accessible.

This change fulfills the requirement to "stop" the path protection demo while maintaining the workflow structure for potential future re-enablement if needed.

This commit introduces a new procedural level generation framework based on a 'physics-first' philosophy. Instead of generating random geometry and testing for solvability, this new system guarantees a traversable path by design.

Key features of this implementation include:

- **PlayerCapabilitiesProfile:** A new class to decouple the generator from the game's specific player physics.
- **Grid Class:** A robust class for managing tilemap data with boundary checks.
- **Physics-Aware Path Carving:** A new `generateSimpleRoom` function implements an agent-based algorithm that carves a provably valid path through a solid grid. It uses physics helper functions (`canReach`, `getJumpTrajectory`) to simulate player movement and ensure the path is traversable.
- **Phaser Integration:** The `GameScene` has been refactored to use the new generator. It now creates a tilemap from the generator's output, complete with collision handling.
- **Updated Tests:** The Jest tests for `GameScene` have been updated to reflect the new architecture and ensure the integration is working correctly.

This new system provides a solid and extensible foundation for future level generation work.

author: d4vinci
body: # Release Notes v0.3.2 ## 🚀 New Stuff - **Optional fetcher dependencies**: All fetchers are now part of optional dependency groups, reducing core package size. So the base `scrapling` module is now the parser only, and to use the fetchers or the commandline options, you have to do: `pip install "scrapling[fetchers]"`. Check out the detailed installation instructions from [here](https://scrapling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/#installation) - **Per-page configuration in sessions**: Session classes for browser fetchers now support individual configuration per page in sessions. All fetch-level parameters are now validated like session-level ones. More details on the documentation website [here](https://scrapling.readthedocs.io/en/latest/fetching/dynamic/#full-list-of-arguments) - **Improved browser-based fetchers** - A new option to control whether to wait for JavaScript execution to finish in pages or not (it's enabled by default now, as it was before) - The Stealth mode is now more reliable in `DynamicFetcher` and its session classes. - Both `DynamicFetcher` and `StealthyFetcher` are now using fewer resources (Automatically finding and closing the default tab opened by Persistent contexts in Playwright API) - Fixed a vital logic bug in browser-based fetchers' pages rotation - previous pages are now replaced with fresh ones. (Tabs that get reused in rotation are possibly contaminated from previous settings used on them) - `StealthyFetcher` and its session classes are now slightly faster (5%) - **Enhanced `.body` property**: Now returns the passed content as-is without processing, enabling file downloads and handling non-HTML requests. Below is an example of downloading a photo: ```python from scrapling.fetchers import Fetcher page = Fetcher.get('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/D4Vinci/Scrapling/main/images/poster.png') with open(file='poster.png', mode='wb') as f: f.write(page.body) ``` ## 🐛 Bug Fixes - **Encoding issues resolved**: Fixed multiple encoding problems that happened with some websites in parser, mcp mode, and extract commands (Also solves #80 and #81) - **Faster parsing**: Due to many changes here and there, the library is now faster, and it's reflected in the updated benchmarks ## 🔨 Misc - **Updated benchmarks**: Refreshed performance benchmarks to compare the current speed improvements to the latest versions of similar libraries - **Refactored a lot of the code and replaced dead code with better implementations**: Fewer code, cleaner code, easier maintenance - **Added YouTube video**: Included video content for MCP documentation. - **A new issues template**: Easy new template for users who can't use the current templates. - **CI workflow optimization**: Tests workflow now skips runs when only documentation or non-code files are changed. - **Updated dependencies**: Bumped up various dependencies to the latest versions. - **Code style improvements**: Applied new ruff rules across all files. - **Pre-commit hooks**: Updated pre-commit configuration. ## 🎯 Breaking Changes - Removed `max_pages` parameter from sync `StealthySession` to match `DynamicSession` (it's meaningless to have in the sync version) _🙏 Special thanks to our [Discord community](https://discord.gg/EMgGbDceNQ) for all the continuous testing and feedback_ --- ### Big shoutout to our biggest Sponsors

body:
This PR implements a complete flashcard application with spaced repetition functionality as requested in the issue. The application helps users study and memorize information efficiently using the scientifically-proven spaced repetition technique.

## Features Implemented

### Core Functionality
- **Interactive Flashcard Interface**: Clean, modern web interface with card flip animations
- **Spaced Repetition Algorithm**: Full implementation of the SM-2 (SuperMemo 2) algorithm that optimizes review intervals based on user performance
- **Three-Tier Difficulty Rating**: Users can rate their performance as "Again (Hard)", "Good", or "Easy" to adjust future review scheduling
- **Progress Tracking**: Real-time statistics including success rate, study streaks, and cards reviewed
- **Local Data Persistence**: All flashcards and progress are saved in browser local storage

### User Experience
- **Responsive Design**: Works seamlessly on both desktop and mobile devices
- **Intuitive Navigation**: Three main sections - Study, Manage Cards, and Statistics
- **Keyboard Shortcuts**: Efficient studying with spacebar to show answers and number keys (1-3) to rate difficulty
- **Sample Content**: Includes sample flashcards for immediate testing and demonstration

### Technical Implementation
- **Pure Web Technologies**: Built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript - no external dependencies
- **Modern JavaScript**: Uses ES6+ features including classes, arrow functions, and template literals
- **CSS Grid & Flexbox**: Responsive layout system that adapts to different screen sizes
- **SM-2 Algorithm**: Proper implementation of the spaced repetition algorithm with interval calculations and e-factor adjustments

## How It Works

The spaced repetition system automatically schedules card reviews based on how well you know each card:
- Cards you struggle with appear more frequently
- Cards you know well appear less frequently over time
- The algorithm maximizes long-term retention while minimizing study time
